detail.longDescription: I am running Python 3.13.14 on Windows 11, using VS Code 1.100.3 with the ms-python extension, inside a conda environment managed by Miniforge3. matplotlib version is 3.11.1, PyQt5 (pyqt 5.15.11) is installed. I am running scripts from the PowerShell terminal, not from a Jupyter notebook or the VS Code integrated debugger. The problem is that plt.savefig() silently kills the process with exit code 1 after plt.plot() completes successfully. No exception is raised, no traceback is printed, and the try/except block catches nothing. The output file is never written. I can reproduce the issue exactly with this one-liner run directly from PowerShell: & C:\Users\tziokas.conda\envs\bo-xgb\python.exe -c "print('start'); import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg'); print('matplotlib OK'); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt; print('pyplot OK'); plt.figure(); print('figure OK'); plt.plot(r_2_python_conv...codes.docx +2 ); print('plot OK'); plt.savefig(r'H:\list_data\python_version_list\test_plot.png'); print('saved OK')" The output is: start matplotlib OK pyplot OK figure OK plot OK then the process exits with code 1. The line print('saved OK') is never reached, meaning the crash happens inside plt.savefig() itself, not during import, figure creation, or plotting. The same behaviour occurs when the code is saved as a .py file saved as UTF-8 without BOM with CRLF line endings: import matplotlib matplotlib.use("Agg") import matplotlib.pyplot as plt try: plt.plot(r_2_python_conv...codes.docx +3 ) plt.ylabel("some numbers") plt.savefig(r"H:\list_data\python_version_list\test_plot.png", dpi=150) plt.close() print("Plot saved.") except Exception as e: print(f"ERROR: {type(e).name}: {e}") import traceback traceback.print_exc() Output: nothing. Exit code 1. The try/except catches nothing. What I have already tried: setting matplotlib.use("Agg") explicitly before any pyplot import — no change. Uninstalling and reinstalling matplotlib via conda — no change. Installing PyQt5 via conda in case a missing Qt backend was the cause — no change. Verified all three imports succeed individually in isolation. Verified plt.figure() and plt.plot() both succeed and print their confirmation lines. The output directory exists and is writable. The crash happens specifically between plt.plot() completing and plt.savefig() being called, on the Agg backend, with no exception raised anywhere in Python. Is there a known issue with matplotlib 3.11.x on Python 3.13 on Windows that causes crash during the render or save step specifically?
